question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{3}-1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{3}+1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1} & = \\ \frac{1-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}-1} & = \\ \frac{(1-\sqrt{3})(\sqrt{3}-1)}{(\sqrt{3}+1)(\sqrt{3}-1)} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}-1-(\sqrt{3})^{2}+\sqrt{3}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}-(1)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}-1-3+\sqrt{3}}{3-1} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{3}-4}{2} & = \\ \frac{2(\sqrt{3}-2)}{2} & = \\ \sqrt{3}-2\end{aligned}
$$
